cases.title: A late lead change
cases.takeaway: Kimi leads at T180, but Flash overtakes it at T183 and finishes ahead at T210. The recorded plans move from settlement logistics to growth, research and wonder completion. This trajectory shows why a short horizon can miss a later reversal.

quotes.text: All 4 cities are building Settlers, leaving us completely undefended.
Abandon Bilbao→(3,13) transit — it takes 17 turns and is infeasible before turn 114.
Do not release both garrison Warriors at once.
RECOMMENDATION: Keep 145 in Bilbao, build Valencia Phalanx t183-187. This removes the temporary Bilbao vulnerability.

cases.title: The cost of a late defensive collapse
cases.takeaway: All three trajectories face mounting losses. Flash is eliminated at T186; Kimi retains three cities at T210, while None retains one. Kimi also loses territory and score late in the game, so the contrast is about the timing and extent of collapse rather than uninterrupted success.

quotes.text: Focus on growing 9 existing cities to max happiness and size, stacking tech count, and completing Zeus.
P(fall)=1.00 means Maputo is lost regardless.
quotes.context: The acting agent rejected this assessment and retained a fortification plan.

quotes.text: Wake at t180-t181, not t183; the candidate's by-turn-185 checkpoints can fire after the cities are already gone.
